headline_en: Three including a Bangladeshi killed in shootout with police in Malaysia
summary_en: Malaysian police shot dead three suspected members of a criminal gang called 'Centro Gang', one of them a 38-year-old Bangladeshi, at KM 17 Jalan Pekan-Kuantan in Pahang on Monday 11 March 2024. Police said the gang was believed to be behind gold-shop robberies causing losses of over 4 million ringgit. The two Vietnamese dead had passports and entered as tourists; police were still finding out about the Bangladeshi.

facts.statement: In Malaysia, three suspected members of a criminal group called 'Centro Gang' were killed in a shootout with police at about 11:30 am local time on Monday (11 March 2024) at KM 17 Jalan Pekan-Kuantan; one of the dead was a Bangladeshi aged 38, the other two were Vietnamese nationals aged 36 and 44. Their bodies were recovered from inside a car.

Malaysian police believe the three killed in the March 2024 Pekan shootout, including a Bangladeshi, were involved in several robberies of gold jewellery shops causing losses of more than 4 million (40 lakh) Malaysian ringgit.

Pahang state police chief Datuk Seri Yahaya Othman said Selangor and Pahang police criminal investigation officers spotted a suspicious car in the Pahang State Development Board area in Pekan; the driver refused to stop and drove towards the Jalan Pekan-Kuantan bypass; after a chase, when police tried to search the car, the suspects fired at them and police fired back in self-defence.
facts.source_in_article: Pahang police chief Datuk Seri Yahaya Othman

facts.statement: Pahang police said seven bullets, a pistol, a drill machine, a grinder, sharp weapons and a hammer were seized from the car, and these are believed to belong to the suspected Bangladeshi.
facts.source_in_article: Pahang police chief Datuk Seri Yahaya Othman, press conference at Pahang police headquarters

facts.statement: Malaysian police said the two Vietnamese killed had passports and had entered Malaysia as tourists; police were still making enquiries about the suspected Bangladeshi (his status was not given), and the shootout was under investigation.

headline_en: Free higher education in China for Bangladeshi students: how to apply
summary_en: Applications are open for the Chinese Government Scholarship for the 2027-28 academic year for Bangladeshi students, Type A category, through the Chinese embassy in Bangladesh; deadline 10 January 2027. The scholarship is fully funded (tuition, free dormitory, monthly living allowance, return airfare). The article lists age limits and the online application steps, including agency number 0501.

facts.statement: The Chinese Government Scholarship for the 2027-28 academic year is open to Bangladeshi students under the Type 'A' category through the Chinese embassy in Bangladesh, for bachelor's, master's, PhD and general and senior research or training (scholar) programmes.
The last date to submit applications for the 2027-28 Chinese Government Scholarship (Type A, via the Chinese embassy in Bangladesh) is 10 January 2027.

Under the Chinese Government Scholarship, subjects available include engineering, IT, artificial intelligence, medicine, agriculture, environment, business administration and social sciences; conditions may differ by university, subject and language of instruction.

Eligibility for the Chinese Government Scholarship (Type A, Bangladesh): good academic results and required physical fitness; age generally under 25 for bachelor's, under 35 for master's, under 40 for PhD; age limit 45 for the general scholar programme and 50 for the senior scholar programme.
The Chinese Government Scholarship is fully funded: full tuition fee waiver, free accommodation in a university dormitory, a monthly living allowance, and return airfare between Bangladesh and China.

To apply for the Chinese Government Scholarship, register on the official Chinese Government Scholarship website and apply online; choose 'Type-A' as the programme type and use agency number '0501'; then enter personal information, education, preferred university and subject, upload required documents and submit; interviews or other selection steps may be required as the authority instructs. Detailed instructions are on the Chinese embassy website.

headline_en: Germany makes the visa process easier for Bangladeshi students
summary_en: The German embassy in Dhaka is introducing the digital Consular Services Portal (Auslandsportal) for bachelor's and master's student visa applications from 1 January 2027, to cut long appointment waits. Applicants will fill forms and upload documents online before attending, with preliminary document checks through VFS. Those already on the old appointment waiting list must open an account on the new portal and apply again.

facts.statement: From 1 January 2027, the German embassy in Dhaka will take bachelor's and master's student visa applications through the digital 'Consular Services Portal' (Auslandsportal), where students fill in the application, submit documents and check the latest status online.

Under the new German student visa system (from 1 January 2027), applicants fill in the form and upload required documents online before appearing in person at the embassy, and can have their application documents preliminarily checked through VFS; on the appointment day, biometric data collection, visa fee payment and document verification are expected to be done faster.

Once the new Consular Services Portal starts, applicants already on the old German student visa appointment waiting list must apply again: students who registered under the old system must open an account on the new portal and apply afresh.

Under the old German embassy appointment system in Dhaka, students had to wait a long time for visa appointments; the embassy expects the new portal to reduce the waiting time, though it said re-applying may cause temporary inconvenience for those who had waited long.
Application process, required documents and detailed instructions for German student visas are on the new Consular Services Portal (Auslandsportal) and the German embassy's official website.

headline_en: 'Italy-bound thinking' a main cause of poor exam results
summary_en: In Rajoir upazila of Madaripur, where many families have members in Italy, no student at any of the seven colleges got GPA-5 in the 2026 HSC and the pass rate fell to 37.11%. Teachers and education people blame irregular attendance and boys' focus on going to Italy. The district employment and manpower office says 960 people went to Italy officially from Madaripur between June 2015 and October 2026, while a private organisation says over one lakh went irregularly to Italy and Europe from Madaripur in 15 years, over 70,000 of them from Rajoir.

facts.statement: From June 2015 to October 2026, 960 people went to Italy from Madaripur district through official (government-recorded) channels.
facts.source_in_article: Md. Abdul Jalil Mia, Assistant Director, Madaripur District Employment and Manpower Office (DEMO)

facts.statement: According to a private organisation (not named), over the last 15 years more than one lakh people from various upazilas of Madaripur went irregularly (illegally) to Italy and other European countries, of whom more than 70,000 young men from Rajoir upazila went to Italy.
A village in Ishibpur union of Rajoir upazila, Madaripur, is known as 'Italy village' (ইতালি গ্রাম); several thousand young men from this village alone have gone to Italy irregularly.

In Rajoir upazila, Madaripur, many families have a member in Italy; most boys become keen to go to Italy after passing SSC and lose interest in college studies, which education people say is one main reason for the poor 2026 HSC results.

In the 2026 HSC exam, 1,172 students sat from Rajoir upazila's 7 colleges and 435 passed (37.11%); no student got GPA-5; Rajoir Government Degree College's pass rate was 25.27%. In 2025 the upazila pass rate was 40.55% with six GPA-5s; in 2022 68.65% (62 GPA-5), 2023 59.12% (9), 2024 67.44% (26).

Sukdeb Chandra Banik, acting principal of Lundi Government Degree College, Rajoir, said boys in the area are always busy trying to go to Italy and pay no attention to studies, and girls also marry Italy-based expatriate men when they can; 80% of the college's students are girls.

Alik Kumar Dhar, headteacher of Government Rajoir Gopalganj KJS Pilot Model Institution and College, said boys rarely come to college and think 'what is the use of studying? The boy next door went to Italy and is earning lakhs of taka.'

headline_en: Studying at Egypt's Al-Azhar institute: how Bangladeshi students can apply
summary_en: Egypt's government is offering 24 scholarships (18 undergraduate, 6 master's) to Bangladeshi students at Al-Azhar University's Al-Sharif Institute for 2026-27. The Secondary and Higher Education Division of the Education Ministry invited online applications from 3 to 17 November 2026 midnight, with hard copies due at the Bangladesh Secretariat by 3:30 pm on 18 November 2026. The article lists eligibility, documents (attested by the relevant ministry), and how and where to submit.

facts.statement: For the 2026-27 academic year, the government of Egypt will give 24 scholarships to Bangladeshi students at Al-Azhar University's Al-Sharif Institute: 18 at undergraduate level and 6 at master's level. Applications are invited by the Secondary and Higher Education Division of Bangladesh's Ministry of Education.
facts.source_in_article: Secondary and Higher Education Division notice (Scholarship and Engineering University Branch)

facts.statement: Online applications for the 2026-27 Al-Azhar (Egypt) scholarships opened on 3 November 2026 and close at 12 midnight on 17 November 2026; hard copies of required documents must be submitted by 3:30 pm on 18 November 2026.
Applications for the Al-Azhar scholarship must be made in writing, meeting the conditions and following the instructions and guidelines sent by the Egyptian embassy in Dhaka.

Al-Azhar scholarship requirements: basic knowledge of Arabic (Arabic proficiency, and an Arabic proficiency certificate, gets priority in selection); latest academic certificate attested by the relevant ministry; original birth registration certificate showing mother's name and nationality, attested by the relevant ministry; six recent photos; original passport valid for at least six months; police clearance certificate attested by the relevant ministry; a doctor's medical certificate on physical and mental fitness attested by the relevant ministry; and an attested negative PCR test certificate.

To apply for the Al-Azhar scholarship, first apply online through the Ministry of Education's designated link (3 to 17 November, until 12 midnight) following the Egyptian embassy's guideline; then submit a printed copy of the completed form plus attested photocopies of documents including academic certificates and mark sheets, passport photocopy, national ID card, police clearance certificate, Arabic proficiency certificate and other relevant papers.

Hard copies for the Al-Azhar scholarship must be dropped in the designated box in the reception room next to Gate 2 of the Bangladesh Secretariat, Dhaka, between 9 am and 3:30 pm; deadline 3:30 pm on 18 November 2026. Applications submitted anywhere else will not be considered.

The Al-Azhar scholarship application envelope must show sender's and recipient's name and address, the ID or tracking number and the programme name; recipient address: Deputy Secretary, Scholarship and Engineering University Branch, Room 1706, Building 6, Secondary and Higher Education Division, Ministry of Education, Bangladesh Secretariat, Dhaka.
The Ministry of Education asked those already selected for any other government scholarship not to apply for the Al-Azhar scholarship.
Al-Azhar University has more than 30,000 teachers and over five lakh students; 20% of students are foreign, from more than a hundred countries; it has branches in Gaza (Palestine) and Doha (Qatar).

headline_en: Bangladesh writes to Saudi Arabia seeking answers to 6 questions on two executions
summary_en: Bangladeshi nationals Nazrul Islam Abdul Basir and Sweety Akter were executed in the Makkah region on 14 October 2026 as a discretionary (ta'zir) punishment. On 19 October Bangladesh's Consul General in Jeddah handed a note to the Saudi foreign ministry asking six questions: the offence, the attested verdict, the method of execution, where the bodies are, and whether they had lawyers or sought legal aid. Saudi Arabia's prisoner list had named them without their sentences, so Bangladesh could not give consular help; Saudi had not replied.

facts.statement: Bangladeshi nationals Nazrul Islam Abdul Basir and Sweety Akter were executed in the Makkah region of Saudi Arabia on 14 October 2026; the death sentence was carried out as a judge's discretionary punishment (বিচারকের স্বেচ্ছাধীন শাস্তি).

On 19 October 2026 Bangladesh's Consul General in Jeddah, Md. Sakhawat Hossain, met Saudi foreign ministry Director General Farid bin Saad Al Sehri and handed over a diplomatic note (addressed to the Makkah branch of the Saudi foreign ministry) asking six questions about the two executions: the type and nature of the offence, when and where it happened and when they were arrested; an attested copy of the verdict; how the sentence was carried out (public beheading by sword or another method); where the bodies are and whether they will be sent to Bangladesh or were buried in Saudi Arabia; whether lawyers were appointed for them during investigation and trial; and whether either sought legal aid.

Neither Dhaka nor the Bangladesh mission in Jeddah had detailed information about the execution process for the two Bangladeshis, and the mission was not sure whether they had legal representation at trial.

Saudi authorities regularly give Bangladesh lists of jailed and convicted Bangladeshis; the September 2026 list named the two later executed, one charged with 'adultery' and the other with an 'ICT' (information technology) offence, but did not give their sentences, so Bangladesh could not provide consular service without knowing of the death sentences.

According to the Saudi Interior Ministry statement, the two Bangladeshis were punished for violating sanctity by engaging in immoral acts in a mosque complex in Makkah; how this matches the charges on the prisoner list is unclear.

Diplomatic sources said that had the mission known of the death sentences it could have acted to protect the two; in such cases legal aid, appeals and high-level diplomatic intervention are usually attempted.

Foreign State Minister Humayun Kabir told journalists in Dhaka that executing on such charges was disappointing; according to information from Saudi Arabia the sentence was carried out in October 2026 after trial in a lower court and appeal court.

On 30 September 2026 Saudi Arabia sent a list of about 2,500 prisoners which said 22 Bangladeshis, including the two later executed, had been sentenced but did not specify what punishment each received; Bangladesh has written to Saudi Arabia seeking specific information about those 20 others.
As of 23 October 2026 Saudi authorities had not replied to Bangladesh's diplomatic note on the two executions.

headline_en: Visa fraud for 209 Bangladeshis in Canada: case against 5 people
summary_en: On 22 October 2026 the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) announced charges against five people running a visit-visa fraud ring that filed 243 temporary resident visa applications for 209 Bangladeshi nationals using fake Canadian hosts, invitation letters and forged documents. Four accused appeared in court in Quebec; one, believed to be in Bangladesh, faces an arrest warrant. CBSA warned that false information can bring the applicant a 5-year ban even if an agent prepared the application.

facts.statement: On 22 October 2026 the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) announced it had laid charges against five people who ran an organised visit-visa fraud ring using forged Canadian visit visa documents and false information. Four accused were brought before a court in Salaberry-de-Valleyfield (printed 'প্ররভ্যালিফিল্ড'), Quebec: Russell Mirza (রাসেল মির্জা) and Mohammad Aminul Islam of Montreal, Md. Mudassar Alam Bhuiyan of Toronto, and Md. Rakibul Hasan, believed to be in Bangladesh, for whom an arrest warrant was issued; one more associate was found to be involved.

The ring submitted 243 temporary resident visa (TRV, visit visa) applications in the names of 209 Bangladeshi nationals, showing Canadian citizens as fake hosts with invitation letters and using forged documents and false information to obtain visit visas.

The investigation began after a CBSA joint control and inspection operation with local police and fire service at a residential building in Mercier, Quebec on 3 July 2024 found signs of immigration-law violations among residents; a formal investigation started in August 2024. On 3 June 2025 CBSA anti-fraud officers executed search warrants at four locations in Quebec and Ontario, seizing many computers, digital devices and documents; investigators focused on 79 of the visa applications to build the case.

Charges in the Canadian visit-visa fraud case were laid under the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA): sections 117(1) and 117(3) (organising illegal entry into Canada through conspiracy), 126 and 128(a) (knowingly helping create false information and conceal facts in immigration applications), and 131 (knowingly inducing or aiding violation of Canadian immigration law).

CBSA warned that fake bank statements, fake invitation letters or false information must never be used for a Canadian visa; even if an agent or third party prepares the application, the main applicant can face serious immigration penalties including a 5-year ban for misrepresentation.

headline_en: 59 foreigners executed in Saudi Arabia in first 6 months of this year, including Bangladeshis
summary_en: The European Saudi Organisation for Human Rights (ESOHR) recorded at least 108 executions in Saudi Arabia in the first half of 2026, 59 of them foreigners (including Bangladeshis) from 17 countries; 71 were for drug offences. The recent execution of two Bangladeshis in Makkah is not in that count, and how many Bangladeshis were executed in the half-year is not known. ESOHR documents lack of interpreters and legal aid for foreign prisoners on death row.

facts.statement: In the first six months of 2026 the European Saudi Organisation for Human Rights (ESOHR) recorded at least 108 executions in Saudi Arabia, including Bangladeshis and nationals of other countries; 59 were foreigners (about 54%) and 49 Saudis (46%). How many Bangladeshis were executed in that period is not known.

Nationalities of those executed in Saudi Arabia in H1 2026 (17 countries) included Saudi Arabia, Bangladesh, Ethiopia, Pakistan, Sudan, Yemen, Syria, Jordan, Somalia, Egypt, Nigeria, Benin, Iraq, Kuwait, Kenya, Uganda and Afghanistan.

Of the 108 executions in Saudi Arabia in H1 2026: 71 for drug-related offences (66%; elsewhere given as 65.7%), 25 for murder (23%), 9 for political and security cases (8%; also given as about 8.3%), 3 for other offences (3%); 83 (76.8%) were for crimes not involving killing; 84 (77.7%) were ta'zir (judge's discretionary) sentences.
Of the 71 drug-related executions in Saudi Arabia in H1 2026, 49 (45.3% of all executions) were of foreign nationals, most from Ethiopia, Pakistan, Sudan and Yemen.
Drug offences were the largest single cause of executions in Saudi Arabia in the first half of 2026 (71 of 108), and most executions (83 of 108) were for crimes not involving killing.
For 91 of the 108 Saudi executions in H1 2026 (84.2%), ESOHR or other organisations could not learn of or document the case before the execution, showing a continued lack of transparency.
Two Bangladeshi nationals convicted of 'immoral acts' in a mosque in Makkah were recently executed; they are not included in ESOHR's first-half 2026 count.

ESOHR documented violations in death-row cases of foreign prisoners in Saudi Arabia: no professional interpreter, no legal aid, defendants not understanding the judicial process, and no effective chance to defend themselves. Prisoners said death-row inmates were recently isolated for a short time, cut off from the outside world, and then suddenly taken for execution.
ESOHR says many people remain on death row in Saudi prisons, including 58 Ethiopians in Khamis Mushait prison, five Ethiopians and five Somalis in Najran prison, and eight Egyptians in Tabuk prison.
Under King Salman bin Abdulaziz and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, total executions reached 2,000 by the first half of 2026, a record compared with any previous reign.

headline_en: Dhaka asks why punishment details were omitted though the two were on the prisoner list
summary_en: On 19 October 2026 Bangladesh's Consul General in Jeddah asked Saudi foreign ministry DG Farid bin Saad Al Sehri why the 30 September prisoner list named Nazrul Islam and Sweety Akter without saying they had been sentenced to death; the Saudi official gave no satisfactory answer, and Bangladesh sent another diplomatic note. The two, from Brahmanbaria and Tangail, went to Saudi Arabia in late 2022 and worked as cleaners for Al Majal company; they were arrested in August 2023, sentenced by a lower court, upheld by a 13-judge appeal panel, and executed on 14 October. A mission message says 306 Bangladeshis are held in western Saudi prisons on moral-misconduct cases.

facts.statement: On Monday 19 October 2026 in Jeddah, Bangladesh Consul General Md. Sakhawat Hossain asked Saudi foreign ministry Director General Farid bin Saad Al Sehri why the regular prisoner list named Nazrul Islam and Sweety Akter but omitted their sentences; the Saudi official could not give a satisfactory answer. Bangladesh gave a further diplomatic note the same day asking for case details, the steps taken during the trial, and whether they had any chance to defend themselves after conviction.
facts.source_in_article: Foreign Ministry officials; Sakhawat Hossain confirmed the meeting

facts.statement: On 14 October 2026 the Saudi Press Agency (SPA), citing the Saudi Interior Ministry, reported the execution of the two Bangladeshis. On 15 October the Bangladesh consulate in Jeddah sent a diplomatic note to the Saudi foreign ministry seeking details, and on 18 October the note was given again to the Saudi ambassador in Dhaka.

According to the Saudi side, the two Bangladeshis were arrested in August 2023, first sentenced by a lower court, then a 13-judge appeal court panel upheld the death sentences, which were carried out in separate cells for men and women.
facts.source_in_article: Saudi officials, as reported by Dhaka officials

facts.statement: Nazrul Islam (home district Brahmanbaria) and Sweety Akter (Tangail) went to Saudi Arabia in late 2022 and joined Al Majal company (আল মাজাল কোম্পানি) as cleaning workers; they were colleagues at the same company.

Nazrul Islam was detained on 1 August 2023 and Sweety Akter on 2 August 2023. The 30 September 2026 list said Nazrul, held in Jeddah correctional facility, was convicted of a cyber crime / information technology offence, without stating when or what sentence; Sweety Akter was listed in Jeddah women's prison for adultery, with no sentence details.
facts.source_in_article: diplomats in Dhaka, Riyadh and Jeddah; government documents

facts.statement: The Bangladeshi diplomat told the Saudi side that if the Jeddah mission had known from the list that the two had been sentenced to death, it could have acted to protect them.

A Bangladesh mission message sent from Jeddah to Dhaka on 18 October 2026 said no Bangladeshi had previously been sentenced to death in Saudi Arabia for cyber or adultery offences; 306 Bangladeshis are held in prisons in western Saudi Arabia on various moral-misconduct cases, of whom 147 have been sentenced to terms from a minimum of one month to a maximum of 15 years in prison.
In three other cyber-crime cases in Makkah, three Bangladeshis were sentenced to between six months and five years in prison.

Foreign State Minister Humayun Kabir told journalists at the Foreign Ministry on 19 October 2026 that the execution on these charges was disappointing and that there had been a lapse in information exchange and diplomatic communication; Bangladesh had asked Saudi authorities for a detailed explanation.

headline_en: From Ferdous to Imran and Akshay: stars in citizenship and visa controversies in India
summary_en: A round-up of film stars caught in Indian citizenship, visa or OCI-card controversies. Two Bangladeshi actors were made to leave India in 2019: Ferdous Ahmed, whose business visa was cancelled after he joined a Trinamool election campaign, and Gazi Abdun Noor, who had overstayed his visa by about nine months. Bollywood actor Imran Khan was told to leave by 28 October for joining a protest.

facts.statement: In 2019 Bangladeshi actor Ferdous Ahmed, who was staying in India on a business visa, joined a road show and campaign for Trinamool Congress candidate Kanaiyalal Agarwal in Raiganj during the Lok Sabha election; after a BJP complaint to the Election Commission, India's Home Ministry cancelled his business visa and served him a notice to leave India; reports say he was also blacklisted. He returned to Bangladesh.
facts.source_in_article: media reports cited by the article

facts.statement: In 2019 Bangladeshi actor Gazi Abdun Noor was served notice to leave India by the Home Ministry after being seen campaigning for Trinamool candidate Saugata Roy in Dum Dum; reports say his visa had expired on 6 July 2018 but he stayed about 9 more months, which officials treated as a visa violation; he was told to return to Bangladesh and apply for a new visa.
facts.source_in_article: media reports cited by the article

facts.statement: India does not allow dual citizenship; an OCI (Overseas Citizenship of India) card gives foreign nationals some special benefits including residence in India but is not equal to Indian citizenship.

Mumbai police detained Bollywood actor Imran Khan (not an Indian citizen) after he joined a protest at August Kranti Maidan, and served him notice to leave India by 28 October, alleging he violated immigration law provisions by taking part as a non-citizen; his lawyer said he would challenge it in the Bombay High Court, arguing the rules do not bar OCI card holders from protests.

headline_en: 'I want to go abroad for higher studies, so I came to this fair'
summary_en: Report on the 'Study Abroad Fair 2026' organised by Prothom Alo and the British Council at the Bangladesh-China Friendship Conference Centre, Dhaka, on 16-17 October 2026, with over 40 education consultancies. Visitors said they could not find a good consultancy and that going abroad to study is harder than before. An online version ran until 25 October.

facts.statement: The 'Study Abroad Fair 2026', organised by Prothom Alo and the British Council with Eastern Bank PLC as banking partner, was held at the Bangladesh-China Friendship Conference Centre, Dhaka, on Friday 16 and Saturday 17 October 2026, 10 am to 8 pm, offering information on higher education abroad, admission processes, scholarships and application advice; the online fair on the website ran until 25 October 2026.

More than 40 education consultancies took part in the Study Abroad Fair 2026, including AHZ (MH Global Group), BD Expert Education Consultancy, Banglay IELTS, BSC, CHS Education, Dream Study International, Dreambaz, Education Hub, Executive Study, Education Connect Global, Education At, Future ED, Faith Overseas Limited, Go Zayan, Growth Academy Global, Fantasy Global Education, H&H Global Education, Campus Group, H&I Council, International Education Counselling Centre (IECC) Limited, Lumos Global, LVS Global Education Consultancy, Maximus Education and Migration, Mentors, Maps Edu, Brit Academy, Pinnacle Consultancy Group, PFEC Global, Sheba Consultancy, Schengen Edu Limited, Study Solutions, 10 Minute School, UniGlobal, Visa Express, Wisdom and Wems Education and Migration.

Visitors at the Study Abroad Fair 2026 said they could not find a good consultancy; Minhaj Hossain, who works at a research organisation, said he wants to take his family with him while studying abroad and return after the degree; final-year student Raisa Meherin said going abroad to study is harder now than before.

headline_en: UK universities limiting admission of Bangladeshi students
summary_en: British universities are withdrawing offers to students from Bangladesh, Pakistan, Nigeria and others to avoid losing sponsor licences after the Home Office halved the maximum acceptable visa refusal rate under the Basic Compliance Assessment from 1 June 2026. The Financial Times reported that the visa application withdrawal rate (as the article words it) for Bangladeshi students rose from 7.1% to 23.5% in the first half of 2026. Prothom Alo found at least 42 UK institutions restricting Bangladeshi admissions, 20 specifically for Sylhet-region students; a consultant said about 20 of his students lost sponsorship after being called for UKVI interviews.

facts.statement: According to a Financial Times analysis of Home Office data (reported 10 October 2026), in the first six months of 2026 the rate the article calls the UK student 'visa application withdrawal rate' (ভিসা আবেদন প্রত্যাহারের হার; the article's opening otherwise speaks of visa refusals) was 40.9% for Pakistani students (3% a year earlier), 23.5% for Bangladeshi students (up from 7.1%), 22.7% for Nigerians (up from 4.5%), and 10.5% for all countries combined (up from 2.3%). Bangladesh ranked second.
facts.source_in_article: Financial Times, citing Home Office data

facts.statement: From 1 June 2026 UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI) applies a stricter 'Basic Compliance Assessment' to universities: the maximum acceptable international student visa refusal rate is cut from below 10% to below 5%; the minimum rate of visa holders completing enrolment is raised from 90% to 95%; the minimum course completion rate, currently 85%, becomes 90% from June 2027. Under a new red, amber and green rating, failing institutions may have to take corrective action and serious or repeated failure risks loss of sponsor licence.

Prothom Alo reviewed two lists based on the experience of agencies recruiting international students for the UK and found at least 42 British universities, campuses and institutions with full, regional or course-based admission restrictions for Bangladeshi students: 22 have stopped or limited admission from various regions of Bangladesh and 20 have separate restrictions specifically on students from the Sylhet region; some restrict only certain courses or campuses.
facts.source_in_article: Prothom Alo review of agency lists

facts.statement: UK institutions listed as limiting or stopping Bangladeshi admissions include Middlesex University, Keele University, De Montfort University, University of East London, University of Roehampton, University of Sunderland, Coventry University and University of Bradford. Those with separate restrictions on Sylhet-region students include University of Chester, University of Wolverhampton, Canterbury Christ Church University, University of Brighton, Cardiff Metropolitan University, Oxford Brookes University and University of Portsmouth.
facts.source_in_article: agency lists reviewed by Prothom Alo

facts.statement: Professor Steven McGuire, Deputy Vice-Chancellor of the University of East Anglia, told the Financial Times his institution has begun withdrawing offers to students from several countries because visa refusals rose.

For the September 2026 intake, many students who applied for UK visas were called for interviews by UKVI; when the university was told of the interview it reassessed the application and withdrew the admission sponsorship (CAS). About 20 students of Global Admission were affected, and the consultant claimed several hundred Bangladeshi students faced the same problem in the September intake.
facts.source_in_article: Mohammad Mustafizur Rahman, Senior Recruitment Consultant, Global Admission

facts.statement: Because of the Home Office's new compliance system, UK universities are checking students' eligibility, language ability and financial capacity much more strictly than before.

Higher tuition fees, depreciation of the taka against the pound, and higher accommodation and visa costs in the UK are putting heavy financial pressure on Bangladeshi students, and many are choosing countries other than the UK.
facts.source_in_article: Md. Mabrur Ahmed, International Student Adviser (Sylhet region), Global Admission

facts.statement: The Home Office says that although international students contribute positively to the UK economy, universities must select students more responsibly to protect the credibility and order of the immigration system.

headline_en: Special courts will be set up for expatriates: Law Minister
summary_en: At RMMRU's 30th anniversary event in Dhaka on 13 October 2026, Law Minister Md. Asaduzzaman said migrants facing harassment can get primary legal aid from the government by calling a hotline, and that special courts for expatriates are being set up at divisional level to hear only migrants' cases. He described long bathroom queues and early starts he saw among workers on a recent visit to Dubai and said Bangladeshi workers earn much less than workers from other countries.

facts.statement: Law Minister Md. Asaduzzaman said on 13 October 2026 that expatriates facing various kinds of harassment can get primary legal aid from the government by calling a hotline (the number was not given in the article).

The Law Minister said special courts (প্রবাসী আদালত) are being set up to resolve expatriates' legal problems; setting them up at divisional level is under process, expatriates' cases will be heard only in these courts, and he hoped it would be implemented soon.

The Law Minister said that on a visit to Dubai a few days earlier he saw workers' inhuman toil: long queues for the bathroom in the morning, leaving for work well before the scheduled time, and calling family after returning from a full day's work; he said Bangladeshi workers are paid much less than workers from other countries despite such hard work.

The statements were made at the 30th anniversary of the Refugee and Migratory Movements Research Unit (RMMRU) and 'Sonar Manush Sommilon 2026' at a Dhaka hotel, chaired by RMMRU adviser C R Abrar; President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir was due to attend the closing on 14 October.

headline_en: Bangladesh a global model for poverty reduction combining social protection and employment: Rashed Al Mahmud Titumir
summary_en: At a regional conference at Chulalongkorn University in Bangkok, the PM's finance and planning adviser Rashed Al Mahmud Titumir said Bangladesh can be a model for poverty reduction by drawing on overseas employment, women's work in garments and social protection. The bulk of the article concerns social protection programmes and Oxfam inequality figures; overseas work appears only as a general statement.

facts.statement: Rashed Al Mahmud Titumir, the Prime Minister's adviser on finance and planning, said in Bangkok on Friday 9 October 2026 that linking Bangladesh's large workforce to labour markets in the Middle East and Gulf countries has created opportunities to increase overseas employment and remittances.

headline_en: 'Five, it has to be five, that's VP Nur's order': Jubo Odhikar president expelled after phone call leaks
summary_en: An audio recording spread on social media on 5 October 2026 in which Lakshmipur district Jubo Odhikar Parishad president Faruk Hossain is heard demanding money from a person wanting to go abroad for passport work, visa, police clearance and BMET card; a party source said he demanded BDT 5 lakh. He was expelled the same night. Expatriates' Welfare State Minister Nurul Haque Nur said police were asked to take legal action; Faruk claims the audio was AI-altered and that he asked BDT 5,000 for a passport.

facts.statement: In an audio recording that spread on social media on 5 October 2026, Faruk Hossain, president of Lakshmipur district Jubo Odhikar Parishad, is heard demanding money from a person wanting to go abroad as initial costs for passport work, visa, police clearance and the BMET card, saying 'five, it has to be five, this is VP Nur's order'; a party source said he demanded BDT 5 lakh (five lakh taka) for these.

On the night of Monday 5 October 2026, Jubo Odhikar Parishad expelled Faruk Hossain and relieved him of all organisational duties, in a notice signed by central office secretary Naim Hossain on the orders of central president Nadim Hasan and general secretary Muntajul Islam; Muntajul said the decision followed preliminary verification of the audio.

Expatriates' Welfare State Minister and Gono Odhikar Parishad president Nurul Haque Nur posted on Facebook that nobody can get away with extortion using his name, and that besides the expulsion the Lakshmipur Superintendent of Police had been asked to take legal action against the accused.

Faruk Hossain denied the allegation, claiming a local group used AI to edit his voice; he said a younger acquaintance named Sakib from his area asked him to arrange a passport and he asked BDT 5,000, which was distorted into five lakh taka.

headline_en: Bangladeshi youth killed in Houthi attack on Aramco facility in Saudi Arabia
summary_en: Md. Sajib Hossain, 26, from Brahmanpara, Cumilla, was killed on 4 October 2026 when a missile or drone fired by Yemen's Houthis hit an Aramco facility in the Al Khurais area of Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province. The Foreign Ministry condemned the attack; the Bangladesh embassy in Riyadh contacted his family and employer and is coordinating with Saudi authorities to repatriate the body. His father and brother, also in Saudi Arabia, will lead the repatriation.

facts.statement: On Sunday 4 October 2026, Bangladeshi expatriate Md. Sajib Hossain (26), from Brahmanpara upazila, Cumilla, was killed by a missile or drone fired by Yemen's Houthi armed group at an Aramco oil company facility in the Al Khurais area of Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province.

The Bangladesh embassy in Riyadh contacted Sajib Hossain's family and his employer, is providing all necessary assistance, and is coordinating with Saudi authorities to send his body home after formal procedures.
Brahmanpara UNO Munni Islam said Sajib, his brother and their father all lived in Saudi Arabia, and the father and brother there would take the main initiative to bring his body home.
facts.source_in_article: Munni Islam, Upazila Nirbahi Officer, Brahmanpara

headline_en: Fulbright Visiting Scholar in the US: teaching and research for Bangladeshis, deadline extended
summary_en: The deadline for the US Fulbright Visiting Scholar Program (2026-27 call, exchange starting September 2027) was extended from 3 October to 31 October 2026, 10:59 am Bangladesh time. The fully funded grant is for experienced Bangladeshi professionals, university teachers and researchers (10+ years' experience, PhD or equivalent) to research or teach at a US institution for one academic year. The article lists benefits, priority fields and the contact email.

facts.statement: The application deadline for the Fulbright Visiting Scholar Program was extended from 3 October 2026 to 31 October 2026; applications must be made by 10:59 am Bangladesh time on 31 October 2026. The exchange programme starts in September 2027.

The Fulbright Visiting Scholar grant funds one academic year of research and teaching at a US institution for experienced Bangladeshi government and private professionals, university teachers and researchers with 10 or more years of professional experience and a PhD or equivalent professional degree; applicants must have English proficiency to work professionally at a US university.

Fulbright Visiting Scholar proposals are invited in all education-related fields with special priority on university administration and curriculum development, distance learning, educational technology, public health, biology, pharmacy, climate change and disaster management, urban planning and international relations; some short-term grants are also offered.

Fulbright Visiting Scholar benefits: travel including return airfare; teaching and related academic fees; monthly stipend for room, accommodation and incidentals; book allowance; health and accident insurance; travel allowance and excess baggage allowance.
To apply for the Fulbright Visiting Scholar Program, create a login account on the online application form link; full instructions are at the link.
For more information on the Fulbright Visiting Scholar Program, contact dhakausexchanges@state.gov.
Over the past 52 years more than two hundred Bangladeshis have taken part in the Fulbright Visiting Scholar exchange programme.

headline_en: Children bought and sold in the name of adoption; bargaining on Facebook
summary_en: A Prothom Alo investigation of 39 public Facebook groups (12 August to 16 September 2026) found babies offered and sought for money in the name of adoption, outside law and oversight, and a Jatrabari company brokering adoptions for a fee. Some posters sought babies to take to Italy or Australia. Bangladesh has no general civil adoption law; the 2026 Prevention and Suppression of Human Trafficking and Migrant Smuggling Act treats adoption for dishonest purposes as exploitation. The article is mainly about domestic child sales.

facts.statement: Bangladesh's 2026 Prevention and Suppression of Human Trafficking and Migrant Smuggling Act (মানব পাচার ও অভিবাসী চোরাচালান প্রতিরোধ ও দমন আইন, ২০২৬) includes adoption for a 'dishonest purpose' as exploitation; sections 372 and 373 of the 1860 Penal Code provide strict punishment for selling, buying or transferring a child for illegal or immoral use.

In Facebook adoption groups reviewed by Prothom Alo in August-September 2026, one woman wrote she would make a deal with a woman five-six months pregnant, pay the caesarean cost and take the baby to Italy; another sought a three-four-month-old girl to take to Australia.
facts.source_in_article: Prothom Alo review of Facebook posts

facts.statement: Bangladesh has no general (civil) adoption law; family laws are religion-based and Muslim family law has no adoption provision. Lawyers say Hindus, Buddhists and Christians can adopt religiously, and anyone can obtain legal guardianship of a child through the family court; under the Children Act 2013, alternative care of disadvantaged children can be transferred through the Child Welfare Board.

Abdul Alim of Kushtia said he was cheated three times in Facebook adoption groups: a woman showed a baby on a WhatsApp video call and asked BDT 10,000 in advance for travel costs; after he sent it via bKash, the Facebook group vanished and all numbers including WhatsApp were blocked.

Al-Bokhari Caregiving Services Limited, Jatrabari, Dhaka (managing director Md. Abdul Ahad) advertised at Dhaka Medical College Hospital to take babies for adoption; its form sets a BDT 35,000 fee from the adopting side (Ahad asked BDT 50,000 verbally), total costs come to nearly BDT 2 lakh, an affidavit agreement is made at a computer shop, and the company does nothing about court guardianship; Ahad said they also provide surrogacy services in India.

DMP Detective Branch Joint Commissioner Syed Harun-or-Rashid said running such child-sale activity on Facebook is a crime whatever the purpose, but the social media monitoring team has not yet brought anyone to book for selling children through adoption groups.

named_actors.name: Al-Bokhari Caregiving Services Limited
named_actors.what_the_article_says: Brokers baby 'adoptions' for a fee (BDT 35,000 on form, 50,000 asked verbally), uses affidavit agreements, no court guardianship; MD Md. Abdul Ahad says it also offers surrogacy in India.

key_quote_bn: ২০২৬ সালের মানব পাচার ও অভিবাসী চোরাচালান প্রতিরোধ ও দমন আইনে ‘অসৎ উদ্দেশ্যে’ দত্তক গ্রহণকে শোষণ হিসেবে অন্তর্ভুক্ত করা হয়েছে।
